title: Borscht
subtitle: Eastern European beetroot soup
excerpt: The great beetroot soup of Eastern Europe: a deep crimson broth built on beef, beetroot, cabbage, and potato, served with a spoonful of soured cream. Earthy, sweet, and unmistakably Slavic.

recipe.sourceNotes: Borscht (Ukrainian: borshch) is the signature soup of Ukrainian cuisine and one of the most recognisable dishes of Eastern Europe, eaten across Ukraine, Russia, Poland, Belarus, Lithuania, and Romania in many variations. The soup is based on beetroot, which gives it its characteristic deep red colour; the other key components vary by region and family tradition but typically include cabbage, potato, carrot, onion, and either beef or pork for flavour. Borscht is served hot in winter (traditionally with a soured cream garnish and a piece of dark rye bread) and cold in summer. The Ukrainian version is the most complex and deeply flavoured, with a long simmer on the beef bone broth and a final vinegar addition to preserve the beetroot's colour.

content.text: The beetroot must be cooked separately from the main broth and added near the end; long-simmered beetroot loses its colour. A spoonful of vinegar added with the beetroot fixes the colour and adds a necessary sharpness to the sweet root vegetables. Serve with soured cream and dark bread.

items.preparation: in one piece; for the broth

content.text: Cover the brisket with 2 litres of cold water. Bring to the boil, skim thoroughly, then reduce to a very gentle simmer. Add the bay leaves and simmer for 1 hour.

Fry the onion and carrot in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Add the potato to the broth with the onion and carrot mixture. Simmer for 15 minutes.

Add the cabbage. Simmer for 5 minutes. Add the grated beetroot, vinegar, garlic, and shredded brisket (removed and pulled into pieces). Simmer for 10 minutes. Season well. Serve hot with a generous spoonful of soured cream and a scatter of dill.
